<section class="reader-section cool" aria-label="Project and test terminology">

## Evaluation

A test with defined tasks, answer checks, and recorded results. Often shortened to “eval.”

## Model and deployment

The model produces answers. A deployment combines it with runtime software, settings, and any tools. Changing those conditions can change the result.

## Benchmark

A named collection of tasks and a scoring method. Sharing a benchmark name does not guarantee that two studies used the same questions or rules.

</section>

## Case and scorer

A case is one task in a test. A scorer is the rule or program used to judge its answer. Passing a narrow check does not demonstrate every kind of usefulness.

## Qualification

A check that the testing setup works. Our published reused-case run is qualification evidence, not a general model-ability score.

## Held-out

Tasks kept separate from setup and tuning. They help test performance on cases that did not shape the configuration.

## Post-hoc

Decided or assessed after the fact. Post-hoc task selection can bias a result, so it cannot replace a preselected capability test.

<section class="reader-section warm" aria-label="Evidence and interpretation terminology">

## Historical reference

A previously published result for an older model. It provides context; it is not a new run by this project.

## Comparable

Two results use sufficiently aligned tasks and rules to support a stated comparison. Missing information is not assumed to match.

## Confidence interval

A statistical range expressing uncertainty under a method's assumptions. It cannot remove bias from task selection or make incompatible tests comparable.

</section>
